audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 4-5 and 6 were 'Skill' and 2+ items was given to Kled, contradicting the packet chart, the 56.66% win rate over 616 games, and the page's own why-strings, which say Kled keeps trading through 4-5, that his R beats Yasuo's at 6, and that Yasuo hard-outscales past two items.
audit.why: Kled's window runs from level 2 to first item; Yasuo's is two-plus items of crit plus the flow shield.
audit.corrected: Levels 4-5 and 6 flipped to Kled, 2+ items flipped to Yasuo, in both layers.

audit.why: Kled: W at 2, full re-E at 3, R at 6, Eclipse. Yasuo: Wind Wall rank-ups (25s down to 17s), Last Breath at 6 (70/50/30s), two crit items.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer never names a single Yasuo ability (packet defect) and treats Last Breath as the thing to track, when Wind Wall is what actually decides this lane.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17s and blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds — Kled's Beartrap (Q) is a projectile, and so is his dismounted Pocket Pistol, so a well-timed wall deletes his entire engage. Last Breath is only 70/50/30s but requires an Airborne target. Sweeping Blade (E) has a near-zero cooldown but cannot be recast on the same enemy for a few seconds, which is the real window to stick on him.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall's 17-25s cooldown and projectile-block, and the Sweeping Blade recast lockout, written into the cooldown and interaction fields.

audit.whatIsWrong: The item line says 'Executioner's Calling early — his healing fights your pattern'. Yasuo has no healing anywhere in his kit.
audit.why: Way of the Wanderer is a shield, not a heal, and no other Yasuo ability heals — Grievous Wounds does nothing against a shield. This is boilerplate carried over from a sustain matchup.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal line replaced with the actual answer to a crit bruiser.

edits.before: - Yasuo Last Breath: matchup-defining — His all-in after a knockup. While down, you win. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Wind Wall (W), 17-25s: 4 seconds that eat your Beartrap and your dismounted Pocket Pistol. Bait it, then you own the next 20 seconds. - Sweeping Blade (E) cannot be recast on you for a few seconds — that is your window to stick. - Last Breath (R), 70/50/30s, needs you Airborne.

edits.before: Track Yasuo's Last Breath: His all-in after a knockup. While down, you win. When it is down — Q-pull + W him.
edits.after: Wind Wall (W) is 17-25s and blocks projectiles for 4s — it eats Beartrap and your Pocket Pistol, so feint one out before you commit. His E cannot re-dash through you immediately; that is when you unload W.

edits.before: His all-in after a knockup. While down, you win. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Bait Wind Wall first — it is 17-25s and it deletes your Beartrap outright.

edits.before: That is Yasuo's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Two Steel Tempest stacks make the third cast a knockup, and that is the only way Last Breath reaches you.

edits.before: Start Doran's Blade + pot. Core: Eclipse  (burst + the all-in sustain), then Sterak's Gage; boots Plated Steelcaps. Executioner's Calling early — his healing fights your pattern.
edits.after: Start Doran's Blade + pot. Core: Eclipse (burst + the all-in sustain), then Sterak's Gage; boots Plated Steelcaps early — his crit autos and Steel Tempest are all physical damage.

notes: Two real errors: the chart gave away levels 4-6 and 2+ items against the packet and the page's own text, and the item line recommended Executioner's Calling for 'his healing' when Yasuo heals nowhere in his kit (Way of the Wanderer is a shield). Also flagged for the maintainer: Kled's Q carries a derived 'knockup' flag, but Riot's own description says the target is yanked toward Kled, not made Airborne — so no claim was written that Kled's Q feeds Last Breath. That flag looks like a tooltip-parsing misfire.
